paragraphs: CareLoop Health sells a real-time monitoring and relapse prevention tool for people living with severe mental illness. The company describes a platform that integrates P4 medicine: predictive, preventative, personalised, and participatory.

People using it make daily quick check ins and can draw on a self-management library informed by cognitive behavioural therapy. The system learns a personal baseline in 28 days and then watches for change against it. When something significant shows up, a key worker gets an email notification. Clinical teams work from a real-time panel of their caseload. The company states that early warning signs appear just 3-10 days before relapse.

CareLoop Health says the tool is built on a decade of NHS-led research. Its home page states the approach is validated by five randomised controlled trials. The platform was co-designed with patients, clinicians, researchers and software engineers. Its co-founders hold academic posts, including a professor of health informatics at the University of Manchester. Another co-founder is described as a psychiatrist for over 30 years.
